newsitem.title: UK: NWE jet fuel still subdued but Med perks up.
newsitem.headline: NWE jet fuel still subdued but Med perks up.

text.p: The NWE jet fuel market was still languishing in the doldrums on Friday, but Mediterranean premiums were supported by arbitrage buying, traders said.
"The North is a dog, it's still long and I don't see anything to stimulate it," said one.
Differentials for cargoes were assessed steady at around April IPE gas oil +$23/25 a tonne cif NWE, while barges were pegged at April +20 fob ARA.
Traders said that buying interest was thin and material was on offer out of the main refining centres in the ARA and U.K., as well as Scandinavia and Ireland.
In the Med, Asian buying helping to push premiums higher, and arbitrage opportunities were also seen to the West Africa and Latin America.
"The Eastern arb is opening and shutting, but at least one or two pieces have floated in that direction already," a trader said.
Med cargoes were assessed at April IPE +$8/$10 a tonne for EU-qualified material and +$4/$5 for non-EU material.
April IPE gas oil futures were trading 50 cents up at $169.75 a tonne at 1625 GMT.
